title: Beyond Tomorrow

evidence.note: The Internet Archive metadata dates the film May 10, 1940. A 1940 US film is free only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. I opened the 1968 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volume but could read only its first 100,000 of about 890,000 characters. No Beyond Tomorrow renewal appeared in that portion, which is not a full search. I cannot cite a renewal-absence result. The uploader's public-domain belief is not a rights determination.
This is a sound film. The recorded track normally shares the film's own copyright status, so the score is undetermined for the same reason as the print. I found no separate music-copyright record.
The Internet Archive metadata credits an original story by Mildred Cram and Adele Comandini. I did not find whether the story was published separately or when, so its term is unconfirmed.

The Internet Archive metadata says a colorized version was produced by Legend Films in 2004. A faithful black-and-white copy adds no new US copyright (Bridgeman v. Corel). The colorization, and any added material, can carry its own protection.

editorial:
Beyond Tomorrow, also listed as And So Goodbye, is a 1940 fantasy film directed by A. Edward Sutherland and produced by Lee Garmes. The story is credited to Mildred Cram and Adele Comandini. The ghosts of three elderly industrialists killed in an airplane crash return to Earth to help reunite a young couple. The Internet Archive describes it as a B film built around veteran character actors with a Christmas theme.

I could not confirm the print's status from a primary record. A 1940 film is free in the US only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. I could read only part of one renewal catalog, so the print, score, story and trademark layers stay undetermined. The rights trap is the Internet Archive's own label: the upload says it is believed to be public domain, but that is a belief, not a rights check. Check the 1967 to 1969 renewal catalogs before reusing it.
faq: Is Beyond Tomorrow (1940) free to use?

Not confirmed. It is a 1940 film, so it is free only if its notice was missing or its copyright was not renewed. I could not verify either from a primary record. Check the 1967-1969 renewal catalogs using the links in the dossier. The uploader's public-domain statement on the Internet Archive is not a rights determination.
Does a copy on the Internet Archive prove the film is public domain?
No. Anyone can upload a film to the Internet Archive and label it public domain. The label is not a rights check. The renewal records are what decide it.
